independence_declaration.statement:
I am code-security-reviewer, session d799789e (invocation task T-DG5-RG-SEC-R2). I authored no implementation in the DG5 scope.

Who authored what:
- the P5 product and the RG1 repairs: solution-architect, backend-workflow-engineer, kpi-benefits-engineer, frontend-ux-engineer and transformation-analyst (docs/delivery/handbacks/DG5/);
- the acceptance suites in the candidate: qa-verifier;
- the merges and the re-gate commits: delivery-orchestrator.

Contract note: the assignment file names its task 'T-DG5-REV-SEC-R5', while the invocation reference names T-DG5-RG-SEC-R2. Everything else in the assignment is consistent (candidate, round 2, my id range F-DG5-102 to F-DG5-119, the paths), so I followed it and use the invocation's run id verbatim.

The assignment's pointer to mirror docs/delivery/reviews/DG4/round-20/code-security-reviewer.json does not resolve on this re-gate branch (DG4 reviews here end at round 9). I followed tools/gates/schemas/review.schema.json and my own DG5 round-1 record instead.

What I wrote: evidence under docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG5/code-security/round-2/, this record and its verifications sidecar. I raised no finding, so there is no findings sidecar.

Where I ran things: builds, static checks and all test runs used a disposable, non-shallow clone ($TMPDIR/rv, `git clone --shared`, at freeze commit 7144a19), with node_modules copied in by cp -a. That made the clone's node_modules writable, so Vitest's default config loader worked there; --configLoader runner was not needed. The databases were disposable PostgreSQL 16.13 clusters on ports 26510, 26530, 26550, 26560, 26570 and 26580. My repro tests were copied into the clone, run and deleted. Afterwards the clone's status was clean, and the clone, clusters and test scratch were removed (90-cleanup.log). The validators and candidate.mjs ran read-only in the repository tree. I ran no e2e (browser) suite; those are the QA reviewer's.

HEAD was 7144a19 when I started. During my run, the runner auto-committed the domain reviewer's run evidence as 23b89db (docs/delivery only; candidate ID unchanged; 91-head-moved.log). I did not open those files.

I formed my verdict without reading any other reviewer's round-2 record. Of round 1, I read only my own record and evidence.

summary:
PASS with no new finding. Both of my round-1 findings, F-DG5-100 and F-DG5-101, are CLOSED_VERIFIED on the real stack in en and ar. The candidate sha256:5df44203…186b is confirmed on a non-shallow clone (2203 files), and the product is the old head ac68d1b plus exactly the RG1 repairs.

Checks:
- Typecheck, build, lint, format, openapi:lint (846 operations) and no-cdn all pass.
- Unit tests pass on Node 22 and on Node 24 (2350 + 1746 + 259, with 2 explained skips).
- The integration suite passes twice on a disposable PostgreSQL 16.13, with the locale unset and with LANG=C.UTF-8. Each run: 320 files, 3084 passed, 1 explained skip, 89 migrations, contract 83/83.
- The historical validators for DG4, DG3, DG2 and DG1 and the DG5 register rules pass.
- My contract-generated P5 role sweep (AUD, ADM, ADM_METHOD; 301 tests) passes, with round 1's five judged deviations now pinned as exact expectations.
- The outbox and advisory-lock registries are consistent, and every p5-pending list is empty.

The RG1 csv.ts change does not weaken formula-injection protection. The migration refusal has no false refusals.

Observations, not raised: a pre-P5 web import cycle (DG1); fetchAllPages stops at 2000 items (old F-DG5-125); the dry run returns recipient ids (designed); the 1.59 MB entry chunk.

Residuals (offline PASS): live registry, live CI, a real IdP, and no AI or notification adapters.
